findings: Fail-closed confirmation blocks all deletions when CriticalConfirm fails — checklist_tool.py delete_list catches ImportError, AttributeError, and RuntimeError from CriticalConfirm instantiation and returns an error, preventing any deletion. This blocks legitimate deletions when the confirmation module is broken or misconfigured, not just when the user denies. Add a configuration flag or fallback mode that allows deletions when confirmation is unavailable, or document that CriticalConfirm must be operational for delete_list to work.

Health-check doesn't test vision multimodal path — _validate_groq_model sends a text-only chat completion with max_tokens=1 to verify the model name is recognized. This doesn't exercise the image_url content type that actual vision calls require. If the model exists but doesn't support vision, health-check passes and the first analyze() call fails. Either document this limitation (validation checks model name availability only, not vision capability) or switch to a minimal vision call with a 1x1 pixel dummy image.

Exception tuple may miss network errors from Groq/Gemini clients — analyze() and analyze_bytes() catch (ImportError, AttributeError, RuntimeError, KeyError, Exception) but the fallback trigger specifically checks for model-not-found error strings. Network errors, auth failures, or rate limits from the underlying HTTP client (httpx, requests) may raise different exception types that bypass the string-check fallback logic. Verify what exceptions Groq and Gemini clients actually raise for model-not-found vs other failures, and ensure the tuple is wide enough or the fallback check is robust to different error types.
